title: "Notebooks"

Every section of the workshop has a notebook. Additional notebooks offer
take-home deep dives. They are **English-primary**, and every heading
carries a one-line Spanish summary — *cada encabezado lleva un resumen en
español.*

## How they are built

<span data-language-key="how-they-are-built"></span>

Notebooks 01–11 separate the live session from later study:

1. **Header:** **Practise today** and **Explore later**, with the same outcomes as the slides and handbook.
2. **Contiguous core block:** recall, example, attempt, feedback, checkpoint. Preparation and feedback definitions appear where needed. Work straight down.
3. **Core complete:** keep your explanation and follow the facilitator’s quiz and break schedule.
4. **Explore later:** optional reference material, exercises, and explorers.

Notebook 00 keeps the entry check and pre-work setup; 12 starts with the exit check. The deep dives are listed under **Going further** below. Solutions remain folded: open them after an attempt. Each notebook loads its own data and runs independently.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
The notebooks are committed with **no outputs and no execution counts**. Every
number you see is one you produced. The prose quotes the expected results, so
you can tell whether yours are right. If yours differ, that is worth
investigating rather than dismissing.
:::

## Going further

<span data-language-key="going-further"></span>

These are **not sections**. They are deep dives, handed out as take-home
material. They have no slides, no Kahoot, and no minutes on the workshop clock:
the {{< var workshop.minutes >}}-minute agenda is exactly what it was without
them. 14 and 15 pick up where section 11 stops — section 11 fits CP as one of
four methods and calls the library deliberately as a black box; these two fit it
by hand and then change what "fit" means.

16 connects PCA’s matrix views to satellite land-cover classification, clustering,
and tensor PCA, with Plato’s cave and three animations.

Four groups of sections have a widget beside them. Section 03 has a
[broadcasting simulator](interactive/broadcasting-simulator.html?lang=en) that
lines two shapes up from the right and steps through the stretch, and section 04
has a [reshape and transpose visualizer](interactive/tensor-visualizer.html?lang=en) that turns
its three photographs into cubes, one per byte, and shows what transpose, reshape
and a memory layout each do to the shape, the strides, the buffer and the picture.
Sections 07, 08 and 09 share a
[projection and SVD stage](interactive/linalg-stage.html?lang=en), eight
pictures of one problem: least squares as a projection onto a column space,
a wide matrix's line of solutions, a determinant reaching zero, the SVD as a
circle turning into an ellipse and a sphere into an ellipsoid, the
eigenvectors of a field of arrows, and the two ways the arithmetic fails.
Sections 00, 02, 04 and 09 and Appendix E share an
[audio tensor stage](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en), nine pictures of
one recording and a tenth of three: air measured 48 000 times a second and rounded to 16 bits, the
array that leaves, [one window cut out of
it](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#frame), [the transform that asks that
window which frequencies are in it](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#spectrum),
the window hopping along to build a frequency-by-time matrix, what a
transpose does to a sound, and the two ways that matrix comes
apart — [the best rank-k approximation there
is](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#lowrank) and [the parts you can
name](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#nmf) — you can hear every one of
those. It ends on [the rank-4 batch a model is actually
handed](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#batch): those three recordings
stacked into one array.

## Running them somewhere other than Colab

<span data-language-key="running-them-somewhere-other-than-colab"></span>

The notebooks only need the scientific Python stack. Locally:

```bash
git clone {{< var repo.url >}}.git
cd {{< var repo.name >}}
uv run --group notebooks jupyter lab
```

The `notebooks` group is declared in `pyproject.toml`, and it is read off the
notebooks' own imports rather than written down beside them. `matplotlib` and
`ipywidgets` are in it because the notebooks use plots and interactive widgets.
Both ship with Colab, so a missing one only shows up when you run locally.

`scikit-learn` and `scikit-image` ship the tumour data, the handwritten digits
and the photographs. Some notebooks use only bundled data; others download
data or install packages. The generated table below lists each notebook's
network requirements.
